articles.title: Resignation not admission of wrongdoing, I am innocent: Justice Varma tells Lok Sabha secretariat
articles.text:
Resignation not admission of wrongdoing, I am innocent: Justice Varma tells Lok Sabha secretariat
New Delhi, Justice Yashwant Varma has asserted that he is innocent of the allegations relating to the discovery of burnt currency notes at his official residence and that his resignation as a high court judge should not be construed as an acknowledgement or admission of any wrongdoing or of the findings against him.
In a letter to Lok Sabha Secretary General Utpal Kumar Singh on September 10 – which was circulated among MPs on Thursday – Varma also contended that proceedings for his removal had become infructuous following his resignation on April 9, and any attempt to remove him from office would be without constitutional foundation.
Citing Article 217 of the Constitution and a 1978 Constitution Bench judgment of the Supreme Court in 'Union of India vs Gopal Chandra Mishra', he argued that a high court judge's resignation takes effect by its own force and does not require acceptance by the President or any other authority.
"Upon my resignation, proceedings directed towards my removal from office did not survive and cannot be continued," he wrote, arguing that the constitutional provisions governing the removal of judges apply to sitting judges and not those who have ceased to hold office.
Varma said he had participated in the inquiry before the Judges Inquiry Committee until April 9, when he tendered his resignation to the President with immediate effect.
He also referred to objections he had raised over the manner in which the inquiry was conducted, saying he was reserving his right to challenge the findings.
Declining to furnish comments on the committee's report or participate in any further process, he requested that his letter and its enclosures be placed before members of both Houses of Parliament and that the matter be closed.
The three-member inquiry committee constituted by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla had found all three charges against Varma proved in its report, tabled in Parliament on August 12.
The charges related to his failure to explain the presence, source and ownership of cash found at his official residence, failure to secure and preserve material evidence, and evasive and unsatisfactory explanations during the inquiry.
The controversy dates back to March 14, 2025, when burnt bundles of currency notes were found at Varma's official residence here following a fire.
A Supreme Court in-house committee subsequently examined the allegations, and its findings of misconduct led then Chief Justice of India Sanjiv Khanna to recommend his removal.
Varma, then a judge of the Delhi High Court, was repatriated to the Allahabad High Court, his parent court. He took the oath there on April 5, 2025, but ceased to discharge judicial functions.
Subsequently, nearly 150 MPs moved a notice seeking his removal, following which the Lok Sabha Speaker constituted the three-member inquiry committee under the Judges Act, 1968.
Varma challenged the constitution of the committee in the Supreme Court, but his plea was rejected. He later withdrew from the inquiry, alleging that the procedure lacked fairness or due process.
He had maintained that he was not in Delhi when the incident occurred and that no cash was recovered.
He tendered his resignation on April 9, while the inquiry process was underway. The committee, however, proceeded to complete its inquiry, and its report was subsequently placed before Parliament.
The resignation has not yet been formally notified. Legal experts have maintained that, notwithstanding the absence of formal notification, Varma has ceased to be a judge and Parliament cannot proceed with his removal.
Under the Constitution, Supreme Court and high court judges can leave office either by resignation or through removal by Parliament on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity. The term 'impeachment', commonly used in India to describe the removal process, does not figure in the constitutional provisions governing the removal of judges.

articles.title: Ukraine Wants More Mirage 2000 Fighters. Where Could They Come From?
articles.text:
Kyiv is asking for additional French-made Mirage 2000 fighters that it says the Ukrainian Air Force could put to work more quickly than the Rafales that it also plans to acquire. But the countries still operating the Mirage 2000 — the Rafale’s predecessor — have their own reasons to hold on to them.

Ukraine’s latest appeal came during the 37th meeting of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group in Brussels on November 17. President Volodymyr Zelensky asked for 40 more F-16s, citing the time existing aircraft spend undergoing maintenance and repairs, an issue you can read about here. The sources for these aircraft are already well established, although more could potentially be added. But Zelensky also called on European partners to provide additional Mirage fighters, arguing that they could be put to work more quickly than Rafales, which require more training and preparation. He did not specify how many Mirages Ukraine wants. At this point, however, any single airframe would likely be accepted, whether it can be used in a frontline capacity or only as a source of spare parts.

France has already delivered at least four Mirage 2000-5Fs to Ukraine, from an initial batch of at least six. It has committed to sending two more by the end of 2026, along with ammunition, although it’s unclear if these are additional jets. However, there is no evidence that another country has agreed to release aircraft in response to Zelensky’s latest appeal. At least one Mirage has also been lost in Ukrainian service.

A Ukrainian Air Force video including brief interviews with a Mirage pilot, as well as two members of the ground crew:

As for the Rafale, Ukraine signed a letter of intent last year to buy up to 100 Rafale F4 multirole fighters from France over the next 10 years. As we discussed at the time, there remain glaring questions about whether the acquisition is actually feasible.

The Mirage 2000 family is not one-size-fits-all

The Mirage 2000 was developed as a high-performance interceptor, returning Dassault to the delta-wing layout used on the earlier Mirage III while introducing fly-by-wire controls among other advances. The family subsequently split into markedly different configurations. Of those in service in France today, the Mirage 2000-5F is an air defense fighter, while the two-seat Mirage 2000D is a dedicated conventional strike aircraft derived from the nuclear-capable Mirage 2000N. They have a good degree of commonality, but are by no means interchangeable donor options.

The 2000-5 brought a substantial avionics and weapons upgrade, including the Thales RDY multimode radar, a revised cockpit, and the MICA air-to-air missile. The later 2000-5 Mk II — also known as the 2000-9 in the United Arab Emirates — added further radar, electronic warfare, and mission system improvements, as well as expanded air-to-ground capabilities, making it the ultimate Mirage 2000. Meanwhile, Greece’s Mk II aircraft are very close to the 2000-9, but, as with all variants, still have country-specific equipment and configurations.

Ultimately, a country may operate — or have operated — Mirage 2000s without these having very much in common with Ukraine’s existing force. Radar, weapons, electronic warfare systems, training and maintenance arrangements all affect how useful a prospective donation would be. Adding a significantly different version would be akin to introducing an entirely new aircraft type into service.

France: an established source, still in demand

FlightGlobal’s World Air Forces 2027 directory, used here to provide up-to-date inventories for individual operators, lists 24 Mirage 2000-5Fs and 49 Mirage 2000Ds in active French service. These figures refer to aircraft in day-to-day use; aircraft in long-term storage or undergoing lengthier upgrades are excluded.

The two additional 2000-5Fs promised by Paris are therefore the clearest near-term contribution. But France’s inventory does not suggest a large pool of surplus 2000-5Fs waiting to be released. Nor should the 49 2000Ds be counted as equivalent replacements: they are strike aircraft, not the same air defense configuration already operated by Ukraine, and they still play an important role with the French Air and Space Force.

France could potentially play a more meaningful role as an intermediary — helping identify aircraft elsewhere, arrange refurbishment, provide weapons and support, or facilitate a transfer deal.

Greece: a promising potential source

Greece is the most obvious candidate for a substantial additional European contribution. It has a reported 24 Mirage 2000-5 Mk II fighters in active service. The Greek aircraft are among the more capable export versions of the family, with an upgraded radar and electronic warfare suite, NATO-compatible encrypted radios, and the ability to employ weapons including the SCALP cruise missile. This would give Ukraine another launch platform for the SCALP and similar Storm Shadow, both of which it has employed to significant effect.

There has been sustained discussion of Greece selling or transferring its Mirages, including proposals tied to the acquisition of additional Rafales. In April 2026, reporting described French efforts to encourage a transfer by offering more favorable terms on Rafale purchases. But Athens had not agreed to release the aircraft.

More recent Greek reporting suggests the obstacle remains fundamental: Athens does not want to create a gap in its fighter force before replacement aircraft are secured. A September 2026 report said there was no active process to dispose of the Mirage 2000-5s and that any future transfer would depend on a firm replacement arrangement, including the number and delivery timing of additional Rafales.

Greece remains a plausible source in the sense that its fleet is relevant and has been discussed in transfer negotiations. But even if a political agreement were reached, the replacement question and the condition of individual aircraft would dictate the number and timing of any delivery.

Greece’s older-model Mirage 2000s could represent a separate, if uncertain, source of airframes for Ukraine. Athens originally acquired 36 single-seat Mirage 2000EGs and four two-seat DGs, distinct from the newer Mirage 2000-5s. Fifteen new-build 2000-5 Mk IIs were later acquired, while 10 earlier aircraft were upgraded to the same standard; other older jets received a more limited upgrade that included the ability to employ Exocet anti-ship missiles.

The remaining EG/DG aircraft have since been retired. Some reporting has put the retired aircraft pool at around 18 airframes in storage, but their present condition and availability are unclear. Returning them to operational service would likely require substantial inspection and refurbishment, and possibly further upgrades. However, they may offer a useful source of donor airframes or parts.

Qatar: the outsider

Qatar is an intriguing possibility because it previously operated the Mirage 2000-5EDA and two-seat DDA, similar to the 2000-5F already supplied to Ukraine. Qatar had a fleet of nine single-seat and three two-seat aircraft, equipped with MICA missiles and other weapons, before removing them from use.

The 12 aircraft are unlikely to be ready-to-fly fighters. Their present location, ownership, storage conditions, and technical state are all unclear. Even if some could be returned to service, that would mean a refurbishment and support effort before they could reach Ukraine. In the past, there were reports that the French company ARES (Advanced Redair European Squadron) had acquired the 12 former Qatari Mirages, but this seems not to have materialized.

UAE: the longer-term prospect

The United Arab Emirates has one of the largest remaining Mirage 2000 fleets. Reportedly, it currently has 44 Mirage 2000-9DAD/EAD/RAD aircraft in active use, including 14 two-seat 2000-9DADs.

The UAE’s 2000-9 is a particularly advanced member of the family. The technical feature describes its customer-specific electronic warfare system, encrypted radio, targeting and infrared pods, datalink, and Black Shaheen cruise missile capability.

Abu Dhabi has ordered 80 Rafales, which could eventually create an opportunity to release some of its Mirages. But the transition is not complete, and the UAE still has to maintain its own combat-aircraft capacity. The Rafale order is therefore, at best, a possible longer-term route to surplus aircraft. In the meantime, the UAE badly needs all the fighters it can muster, as it deals with the considerable aerial threats posed by Iran and its proxies.

India, Taiwan, and Peru: fleets that are difficult to release

Other operators have Mirages, but their circumstances make them less promising candidates.

  • India has a reported 44 Mirage 2000H/I fighters and 11 Mirage 2000TH/TI two-seaters. India has invested heavily in the type and its modernization, making a transfer difficult to envisage. Its aircraft also represent an earlier configuration than the 2000-5F Ukraine operates. At the same time, the Indian Air Force is facing a well-publicized fighter shortage. This fact, and New Delhi’s historic close ties with Moscow, make any kind of transfer to Ukraine extremely unlikely.
  • Taiwan has 44 Mirage 2000-5EI single-seaters and nine 2000-5DI two-seaters in the directory. These are members of the Dash 5 family used by Ukraine, but Taiwan relies on them for its own air defense. A transfer would be particularly difficult to justify given that requirement and the looming threat from the Chinese mainland.
  • Peru has 11 Mirage 2000P/DP aircraft reportedly still in use. Its small fleet makes a large transfer unrealistic, although individual aircraft or components might be worth examining as a potential source of support. The situation could change once Peru begins to receive its new F-16s, but that remains some way off.
  • Egypt operates earlier Mirage 2000EM/BM versions, with 15 and four examples reportedly still in service. Any potential transfer to Ukraine would likely involve returning them to France in exchange for deliveries of other French defence equipment. However, like India, Cairo’s relationship with Moscow means this is something far less likely to get approved.

No obvious pool of ready-to-transfer fighters

As this assessment demonstrates, Mirage 2000 options are currently limited, despite Zelensky’s observation that Europe has more Mirages. France is the most likely operator to make (another) commitment to Ukraine, after its recent announcement that it was transferring two additional 2000-5Fs by the end of 2026. Greece has the most relevant additional active fleet, but Athens has not agreed to release it and wants replacement aircraft before giving up its fighters. Qatar’s former aircraft are no longer in active use, while the UAE’s larger fleet is tied to its own transition to the Rafale.

Zelensky’s request is understandable in operational terms. Ukraine already operates the Mirage 2000-5F, and claims to have put it to good use already in the fight against drones and cruise missiles. Clearly, additional examples of the same variant would offer a more straightforward path to integration than introducing another new fighter type. But the wider Mirage family is not standardized, and a transfer of any variant would still require suitable weapons and spares. There are also questions of providing the required maintenance support and trained personnel.

For now, the most realistic prospect is a limited increase through France, with Greece remaining the key question for any larger expansion. The other fleets offer possible leads, but none currently presents a clear, immediate source of additional operational fighters.

articles.title: "You’re right"—LLMs will get climate info wrong if you ask
articles.text:
Many studies over the years have examined how people encounter climate science information. Some focused on the top results that Google surfaced (back when Google was still in the business of serving links), while others examined social media content or newspaper and TV news coverage. With large language models (LLMs) now forming a share of the public information diet, it's worth looking at how they handle climate change.

But there’s no direct way for researchers to look at the information people have seen. It is served ephemerally to individual users, confined to their chat session. A study led by researchers from University College London and the United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) tried to tackle this question from multiple angles, testing LLMs with different prompts and evaluating their output. They started with benchmarks of simple factual questions (benchmarks that might even be in models’ training data at this point) but also analyzed more complex interactions—including when users think they’re right to push back on an answer.

CO2 Q&A

LLM research often faces (no-true-Scotsman-tinged) criticism for focusing on a particular model rather than some other frontier model that may have been released after the experiment concluded. In this case, the study used 33 models, including multiple versions of the major frontier and open-weight models. The flagship frontier models used were Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, Gemini 3.6 Flash, and GPT-5.6 Sol. (You can find the full list in the report.)

articles.title: XXRI-OS explores the lowest end of the Linux desktop
articles.text:
New Linux distros seem to appear daily, but far too few distinguish themselves by being smaller and simpler.

XXRI OS is a fairly new desktop Linux distro. It has a snazzy-looking website, complete with an amusing URL, and along similar lines, its GitHub page has a very heavily formatted README. Nonetheless, this is not another over-complex opinionated slopfest of an OS with built-in AI, bizarre keystrokes, and several proprietary components. It's almost the reverse.

The main download is just 287.4 MB, and that's the full distro, not a minimalist installer that fetches most of the OS over your internet connection. We installed it in a VirtualBox VM. It took 675 MB of disk space, and in the graphical desktop, when we opened a terminal window, it reported just 75 MB of RAM in use with the desktop and terminal running. We are restraining ourselves hard when we say that those are unusually low numbers for the 2020s. We would expect most cut-down lightweight Linux distros to use around five to 10 times as much disk space or memory.

The current release of XXRI-OS is version 2.7. XXRI OS 1.0 came out in May 2025, making this a young project with five published releases already behind it. It also has much deeper roots: it is based on the existing and much older Tiny Core Linux. The Reg FOSS desk last looked at Tiny Core Linux 15 back in March 2024 and the project is still going strong: the latest version is version 17.1.

Tiny Core Linux is a marvel, but there are prices to pay for somehow getting a graphical Linux desktop into a 23 MB download. It runs from RAM and uses its own extension-based package system, which can make adding components and managing updates unfamiliar territory. XXRI OS takes TCL and turns it into a slightly more conventional desktop.

It installs to disk in the usual way, and it includes the core functions that most people would expect from their OS in 2026. It has a file manager, a text editor, a media player, a simple app store for adding further components, and a settings app including an update manager. It even includes its own web browser, and there are both x86-32 and x86-64 variants.

The desktop layout has a floating dock at bottom center, and the icons are unlabelled. To save you some guesswork, though, floating just to the left of the dock is an icon with a grid of dots, which is an app launcher. The icons in that do have text labels underneath, so you can learn which symbol denotes which function from here.

We plan to experiment more with this remarkable little OS and see how well it runs on the oldest, slowest boxes in the Irish Sea wing of Vulture Towers, but we like what we see so far. It's an impressive experiment in how low Linux can go and remain useful. While Tiny Core Linux goes down to Windows 95 levels of resource usage, XXRI OS has a more usable Windows 2000-level baseline. Over a quarter of a century later, that is nearly unbeatable. ®

articles.title: Impacts Of Latest Neptune Missile Strike On Kerch Bridge Seen In Satellite Imagery
articles.text:
TWZ has obtained satellite imagery taken today of the Kerch Bridge. It shows damage from recent strikes to the rail span, as well as the section of the road span that was knocked out earlier in the week. The rail line was hit again just overnight, bringing train traffic across this vital Russian logistics conduit to a halt for a time. Readers can get caught up first on what was already known about the third Ukrainian strike on the bridge in now four days in our initial reporting.

Vantor’s WorldView-1 satellite captured the image, seen in part at the top of this story and below, at 1:51 PM local time. At least two, and possibly three, impact points are visible on the rail span. From what we can see, the damage looks to be limited to only one of the two sets of tracks on the bridge.

A large scorch mark is also seen on one corner of an arch that goes across part of the rail span. However, this damage does not appear to be new based on previous satellite imagery, as well as pictures and video taken at surface level.

“A section of the northern highway bridge, measuring approximately 225 meters [approximately 738 feet], has collapsed with some sections remaining partially submerged,” Vantor also noted to TWZ when it sent the imagery. “No repair efforts were noted on or nearby the damaged bridge; moreover, no shipping traffic was seen in the strait.”

The damage to the Kerch Bridge’s rail span visible in the Vantor image is consistent with Ukraine’s claims to have successfully “struck the railway section … with hits recorded near the arch and on the tracks” with a volley of Neptune cruise missiles last night.

“Our military says the railway tracks were also damaged, but we’re still checking how badly,” a source in Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky’s office told us earlier today. “We don’t know the results yet.”

That the damage appears to be limited to only one of the two tracks is also consistent with reports that rail service across the bridge has now been restored, but only on one line.

It should also be noted that the rail span will likely be significantly harder to destroy than the road portion of the bridge. The rail section has to be designed to handle the heavier and denser loads of trains passing across. This can be seen visually in the differences between the construction of the arches over the rail and road portions.

How disrupted rail traffic across Kerch Bridge remains now is unclear, and speaks to larger issues emerging from Ukraine’s continued strikes this week. The time it takes to inspect and repair even relatively minor damage could have increasingly serious impacts. This could be compounded by repeated strikes that halt trains from crossing in either direction for hours on end.

Beyond the Kerch Bridge, the only other options for getting ammunition, fuel, food, and other supplies to Russian forces in Ukraine are by ferry across the Kerch Strait or by truck and train overland around the Sea of Azov. As we have reported in the past, Ukraine’s mid-range strike drone campaign already holds the land routes under intense fire, severely limiting Russian logistics. Ukraine has also been hitting Russian shipping in the Sea of Azov.

In addition to repeated strikes on the Kerch Bridge, since October, Ukrainian forces have struck at least six bridges along the R-280 highway, the official Ukrainian United24 media outlet reported. This is a major Russian logistics corridor through occupied areas along the western shore of the Sea of Azov. The attacks have damaged transport links connecting Russia’s Rostov region with occupied southern Ukraine, including routes used to supply Russian forces in Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, and Crimea, the outlet noted.

“The Kerch Strait crossing is just one link in the chain that the enemy uses to supply the front lines,” the Ukrainian MoD said today. “Step by step, the Defense Forces are reducing the capabilities of the rest of Russia’s military logistics. According to the results of previous strikes, damage has been confirmed to the road surfaces of three more bridges: on November 15, across the Seversky Donets River in the Pryshyb area of the Luhansk region, and across the Mius River in the Taganrog area of the Rostov region; on November 14, across the Mius Lagoon in the Lakedemonovka area, also in the Rostov region.”

Beyond severely impacting land routes, the Ukrainian strikes on the Kerch Bridge are having a major effect on Russia’s ability to use sea routes.

The collapsed section of the road bridge extended over the main shipping channel linking the Sea of Azov to the north with the Black Sea to the south. The inability of large vessels to pass through for an extended period of time would have its own serious impacts on Russian logistics chains.

“The structures fell directly into the shipping lane,” Ukrainian Shipping Magazine noted. “The Kerch Strait is only 3–6 meters deep, so all large-tonnage traffic between the Black and Azov Seas passes through the narrow 120-meter Kerch-Yenikalsky Canal. This only deep-water passage runs under the central arch of the bridge – that is where the multi-ton debris now lies.”

“The remaining spans are in shallow water, so large merchant and military ships are physically unable to bypass the blockage, the Crimean Wind monitoring channel notes,” the publication added. “The length of the collapsed span is estimated at over 270 meters, and the weight of the steel arch is 5,500–6,000 tons. Clearing it will require specialized equipment and complex underwater work.”

All of this is impacting Russian residents of the occupied Crimean Peninsula, as well. The following video shows Crimea residents lining up for gas after the most recent bridge strikes amid concerns about the stable flow of supplies going forward.

Officials on the peninsula say they will launch free passenger boat services across the Kerch Strait on Nov. 20, according to Oleg Kryuchkov, an adviser to the Russian-installed head of Crimea.

The service will operate between Port Krym in Kerch and Port Kavkaz on Russia’s Taman Peninsula. However, private vehicles will not be transported on the boats, and passengers will not be allowed to carry gasoline in canisters, per Kryuchkov

Kryuchkov also warned that the service would depend on weather conditions. Storms and strong winds could force temporary suspensions several times a week. Local authorities did not specify how many boats would operate, how many passengers they could carry, or how frequently crossings would depart.

Russian officials have pledged to rebuild the bridge. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin told the official Russian TASS news outlet that authorities will determine a timeline for restoration of the bridge within a week. That work would likely be lengthy and expensive under optimal conditions, let alone under the continued threat of new Ukrainain strikes. It took more than two years to build the road span in the first place and even longer to complete the rail portion.

Russian President Vladimir Putin has also now promised significant retaliation against Ukraine over the damage wrought already to Kerch Bridge.

“We will not negotiate after the strikes on the Crimean Bridge,” the Russian leader told reporters in Shenzhen, China, where he is presently attending meetings of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum. “We will respond to these strikes. Our actions will be much more painful.”

As was made clear just overnight, taking out the remaining rail span of the Kerch Bridge clearly remains a top objective for Ukraine.

articles.title: Google will launch Android app verification requirement globally in January 2027
articles.text:
Google announced Android developer verification last year, and despite numerous objections from developers and users, the company is forging ahead. It began blocking the installation of unregistered apps in some countries this fall, and the system is expanding globally soon. Google says it will start rolling out the requirement in all regions in January 2027, and it urges devs who still haven't registered their apps to do so soon.

The apps you download from the Play Store all come from verified developers, and Google's new requirement expands that requirement to apps from third-party sources. Once developer verification is live in your region, you won't be able to sideload apps unless the developer has registered with Google, which is framed as a security measure. Verification requires providing government identification and paying a $25 fee, which will allegedly make it harder for nefarious actors to distribute malware and scammy apps.

In September, Google launched verification in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. Apparently, nothing exploded, so the company is now ready to expand. It previously said verification would go global in 2027, and it's not wasting any time with the January start. It says that verification will reach all devices within "several months."

articles.title: In US, Pak national asks Rahul Gandhi if neighbours can move past ‘blame game’. His reply
articles.text:
In US, Pak national asks Rahul Gandhi if neighbours can move past ‘blame game’. His reply
Rahul Gandhi said said it was impossible for India to hold talks with Pakistan while innocent people continued to be killed.
India and Pakistan can work together but only if Islamabad stops supporting and encouraging terrorism in India, LoP in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has said. Interacting with students at the University of Chicago on Wednesday, the Congress leader said it was impossible for India to hold talks with the neighbouring country while innocent people continued to be killed.
Gandhi was responding to a question from a participant who identified himself as a Pakistani national. He asked Gandhi whether the two neighbouring countries could “move beyond the blame game and work together for mutual benefit” without allowing external factors to exploit their differences.
“There is room, but there is a big problem, which is the support and encouragement of terrorism by Pakistan in our country,” Rahul Gandhi said. “And it is impossible for us to accept our innocent people being murdered and having a conversation with Pakistan. So the moment that stops, then a conversation can potentially begin.”
ALSO READ | Indian economy in dire straits, Rahul Gandhi says in US; BJP hits out
Rahul Gandhi says India has become a ‘side player’ in global affairs
During the interaction, the Opposition leader also criticised the Narendra Modi government's foreign policy, saying India had become a "side player" in global affairs despite its size and international relationships.
Citing Pakistan's role in facilitating negotiations between the US and Iran, Gandhi said India should have been more actively involved in global discussions.
"India, by its size, naturally has a global voice and India should be actively involved in global conversations. But frankly, India has become a side player," he said. "I'm pretty shocked that Pakistan is busy negotiating with the Iranians and the Americans, and India's just looking," he added.
Pakistan played a key mediating role in the US-Israeli war on Iran that began in February. Islamabad hosted US-Iran talks in April and helped relay proposals between the two sides.
Rahul Gandhi said India should reclaim its historical role in global affairs, recalling its leadership of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM). Founded in 1961, the grouping brought together countries that sought to remain independent of the US- and Soviet-led blocs during the Cold War. India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, was among its founding leaders.
ALSO READ | Rahul Gandhi posts ‘Satyam Shivam Sundaram’ after BJP dig; Himanta Sarma hits back
On X on Thursday, Gandhi said he was “pretty shocked” that Pakistan was negotiating with Iran and the US while India was “just looking”. He said India had a long history of independent foreign policy and should play an active role in global affairs.
“India has always had a sophisticated geopolitical understanding, right from independence. We had a mind of our own. Our foreign policy was guided by what benefits India,” he said. “By our size, our history and our relationships, we should be involved in these global conversations. But frankly, India has become a side player. We have stepped back from the stage. We have a voice and a view, but that view is missing.”
“There was already pain in India. The Iran war magnified it, pushing people over the edge. We cannot sit in India and remain unconcerned about what is happening in the rest of the world,” the Congress leader added.
Rahul Gandhi questions Modi's foreign policy
The Congress leader also questioned PM Modi's approach to foreign policy and said international relations should not depend on friendships between political leaders.
"Friendship is not the point. Who gives a damn about friendship? Do you really think that geopolitics is going to work because the guy is your friend? He's leading a structure. He's got a whole economic system under him. He's not going to make decisions based on whether he likes you or doesn't like you. So these are some of the things that disturb me," Gandhi said.
He clarified that he had no objection to leaders maintaining friendly relations but said understanding geopolitical realities and India's position in the world was more important.
"I don't have a problem with being friends with Mr Modi or being friends with leaders. Friendship is not that important. What's important is that you understand what's going on, who you are, and where you fit," he said.
ALSO READ | ‘India sitting on an economic disaster’: Rahul Gandhi at Columbia University; BJP hits back
Gandhi also spoke about the changing global security order, saying the next global architecture would involve several major powers and civilisations rather than being shaped by the West alone.
"The next global architecture will not be built by one civilisation alone. It will be shaped by multiple civilisations, with America, China, India, the Middle East and Russia all having a role to play," he said.

articles.text:
Maharashtra puts non-essential construction on hold in 304 drought-hit talukas, prioritises relief
The Maharashtra government has directed district authorities to temporarily suspend non-essential new construction works in 304 drought-hit talukas and divert available funds for drinking water supply and other drought-mitigation measures.
A Government Resolution issued by the Planning Department on Wednesday said funds under the District Annual Plan (General) must be prioritised to finish incomplete water supply projects, strengthen existing water sources and ensure water and fodder availability for livestock.
Also Read | Maharashtra adds 2 more talukas to drought-hit list; count rises to 310
The state has identified 304 talukas as drought-affected, and the government said immediate measures were necessary to meet the drinking water requirements of citizens, livestock and other essential needs.
District collectors have been directed to review non-essential new projects, including parks, beautification works, new office and administrative buildings, cement roads, drains and other works involving substantial water consumption, and take steps to temporarily defer them in accordance with prescribed procedures.
Funds available for such deferred projects will be reviewed and reallocated to priority drought-relief works in the affected talukas, the GR said, adding that the exercise of reallocation must be completed by December 31.
The government has clarified that ongoing projects should not be stopped indiscriminately.
Authorities must take decisions on a case-by-case basis after considering contractual obligations, public safety, the stage of work, expenditure already incurred and possible compensation or financial liabilities, it said.
Essential works directly related to drinking water availability, strengthening existing water sources, creating necessary new sources, providing water and fodder for livestock, water conservation, irrigation, public health and emergency requirements have been exempted from the temporary suspension, subject to applicable rules and approvals.
The GR also gives priority to completing incomplete pipelines, pumps, electricity connections, storage tanks and distribution systems required to transport water from existing sources to scarcity-hit villages.
"Projects that can be completed during the current scarcity period and provide immediate access to water must receive priority. New projects that cannot normally be completed within the current financial year should not be sanctioned under the special priority framework," it said.
In exceptional cases, essential drinking water, livestock water or water-source creation projects may be considered even if they extend beyond the current financial year. However, the additional financial liability for 2027-28 must not exceed 10 per cent of the approved District Annual Plan outlay for 2026-27.
District collectors have been asked to convene meetings of district-level officials within seven days of the issuance of the GR and prepare an integrated taluka-wise and project-wise action plan within 15 days.
The government has also provided for expedited approval of urgent drought-relief measures. If convening a District Planning Committee meeting would delay an essential intervention, the collector can submit a proposal to the guardian minister, who heads the committee, for approval, subject to ratification at its subsequent meeting.
Collectors will have to review the progress of approved works and submit reports on fund allocation, expenditure and physical progress to the Planning and Finance departments by the 10th of every month.
The GR also mandates the publication of details of sanctioned works, funds, expenditure and progress on district collectorate websites or government portals.
The provisions will apply to the 304 drought-hit talukas and any additional talukas subsequently declared drought-affected or facing scarcity. The order will remain applicable for the 2026-27 financial year.

articles.title: Anthropic throws open doors at $2T valuation as shares pop 34% in initial trading
articles.text:
Welcome to the world of public AI frontier labs: Anthropic is now a publicly-held company with its Thursday IPO, and investors are clamoring for a piece of the pie, for now anyway.

That $83 IPO price didn’t last long, with shares rocketing to $111.50 by the time the public could get their hands on them at the end of the initial auction. That means that the company was valued at around $2 trillion as of the public availability of the 980 million shares it put up for sale, a 34 percent increase over the IPO price.

At just under six years old, Anthropic’s meteoric rise to that valuation has sent investors into a frenzy despite uncertainties surrounding the company’s future profitability. As we’ve noted, Anthropic is on the hook for nearly $1 trillion in compute obligations that could drag its profitability prospects down if any one of a number of scenarios happens to materialize.

Amodei was on hand to address some of those questions with CNBC this morning following the opening of markets on his company’s big day.

When asked about the risk Anthropic’s massive compute bills to its bottom line, Amodei admitted the company’s needs are difficult to predict, and that - get this - they try to err on the low side.

That’s right: The $900 billion in infrastructure and compute commitments that Anthropic revealed in a recent regulatory filing, which could end up surpassing $1T in short order, might just be an underestimate of what the company will need in coming months and years.

Not to worry, though, the Anthropic CEO insisted: It’s worth it.

“We’re willing to put into place these very large compute spends because, historically, we’ve seen that it pays off,” Amodei told CNBC’s Ross Sorkin, adding that the returns on the cognitive capabilities of its new models are “so high” as to make all that spending worth it - eventually, one would assume based on his comments, Anthropic is sure to come out on top.

But what of the threat of open models that could undermine the constant push at Anthropic and other frontier labs to create the most power-hungry, resource-intensive, and powerful AI? Bah, that’s not a problem either.

Frontier model makers like Anthropic, Amodei said, have already proven that they can do the heavy lifting at the bleeding edge, so you can trust it to make reliable models that are cheaper and less capable, too.

“Anthropic can compete both at and away from the frontier,” The Anthropic CEO said.

Whether that’ll mean long-term success for investors is another thing altogether. Mozilla president Mark Surman doesn’t think valuation translates into long-term success, for one. He told The Register this morning that the one thing he consistently hears from developers is that they want AI they can control, not rent from a frontier lab. As Amodei suggested in his comments, Anthropic is aware that those with less intense AI needs might not choose its models, and that could harm the company.

“Pushing AI toward open source matters so much right now,” Surman said in an email. “Mozilla’s own research this year found that open source models account for a third of all tokens, while the gap with the best closed models is down to about 3.3 per cent.”

In other words, keep an eye on that Anthropic stock - it might be hot now, but reality could still catch up to the company with the biggest-ever IPO.

“The market is already moving,” Surman said. “No valuation changes that.” ®

articles.title: NAND prices tipped to fall as Chinese cloud giants cut SSD orders
articles.text:
NAND flash prices could start falling next year as Chinese cloud operators cut enterprise SSD orders, helping push the market toward oversupply.

Taiwan-based market intelligence firm TrendForce says Chinese cloud service providers are grappling with GPU shortages, high inventories, and fierce competition over AI token pricing.

As a result, they have reduced their total enterprise SSD orders for 2027 by a substantial amount. Although TrendForce doesn't specify any figures, it says the cutbacks in China are large enough to outweigh the additional demand coming from US-based cloud operators.

But don't get too excited: TrendForce forecasts overall NAND flash contract prices falling by 0-5 percent quarter on quarter in early 2027, with all product categories entering a downturn from the second quarter.

Falling orders are only half the story. Manufacturers are also increasing output, while weaker consumer electronics sales could further depress demand.

Strong demand for high-performance storage in the US continues to drive manufacturers to expand capacity and upgrade to newer process technologies. At the same time, the rising adoption of quad-level cell (QLC) technology and increasing number of layers in the NAND chips will further boost bit output, TrendForce observes.

Some suppliers may go slower on their expansion plans in response to sluggish consumer demand, but the firm still expects global NAND flash output, measured in storage capacity, to grow by 25 to 30 percent in 2027.

US restrictions on access to advanced AI chips could put Chinese cloud operators under further pressure. The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has introduced new restrictions on sales of GPUs, and on remote access to them via the cloud.

The new restrictions "set everyone back in China," as The Register reported.

TrendForce adds the caveat to its forecast that its market outlook depends on factors such as the pace of inventory reduction among Chinese CSPs, further changes to the restrictions on overseas GPU procurement, and whether device makers continue reducing storage capacities in 2028.

Sadly, cheaper NAND wouldn't resolve the separate squeeze on DRAM supplies. The situation, caused by memory makers opting to produce high-margin products for the AI market rather than mainstream chips, has already increased prices of PCs in Europe by double-digit percentages, leading to a fall in shipments as buyers balk at the cost. ®

Five Samawajwadi Party workers and one JCB operator was named in an FIR as a 14-year-old boy died after being hit by a bulldozer in Uttar Pradesh's Gorakhpur on Wednesday.
The incident has sparked a massive political controversy with the BJP targeting the Samajwadi Party over alleged lapses in the management of Akhilesh Yadav's roadshow near the accident site and Yadav claiming that his rally was nowhere close to where the incident occurred.
However, an FIR on the incident names a JCB operator, and five SP workers – identified as Sadhu Yadav, Manoj Yadav, Mrityunjay Yadav, Yogesh Yadav and Chandra Prakash.

Teen hit on way to pick up sister

Union home minister Amit Shah says Kashmir has no India-born terrorists for the first time in 35 years after the killing of Lashkar-e-Taiba’s Lateef Bhat.
A day after security forces killed Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorist Lateef Bhat in Kulgam, Union home minister Amit Shah said Kashmir was free of India-born terrorists for the first time in 35 years, terming it a “significant milestone”.
Shah’s announcement assumes significance against the backdrop of over three-decades of militancy in Jammu and Kashmir, in which Pakistan-backed terror outfits including Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM) among others, have recruited local youth to run their networks and carry out attacks on security forces and civilians.
The home minister was speaking at the inaugural session of the two-day counter-terrorism conference of the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in Delhi, which is being attended by senior police officers from the states and Union Territories, officers from counter-terrorism agencies, and experts from related fields including law, forensics and technology. Union home secretary Govind Mohan and Director Intelligence Bureau (IB) Mahesh Dikshit were present at the conference.
Deep Dive
“Yesterday, we achieved a significant milestone in the fight against terrorism. With the elimination of LeT terrorist Lateef Bhat, the entire Kashmir has become free from the presence of India-born terrorists. This situation has come about after 35 years,” Shah said. The development, he said, was the outcome of the government’s sustained efforts and its zero-tolerance policy towards terrorism.
“Some successful operations have recently been carried out against terrorism, which has strengthened the confidence of our country,” he added.
Shah asserted that government was working towards establishing a police station level system across the country for a unified strategy to counter terrorism.
He noted that police forces of different states had made various kinds of efforts, but a lack of coordinated action was visible. “Over time, during the tenures of successive governments, gradual efforts were made to overcome these shortcomings. Today, we can say with satisfaction that in this vast country — from Kashmir to Kanyakumari and from Dwarka to Kamakhya — we are putting in place a system under which a uniform strategy to combat terrorism will operate right down to the level of every police station,” he said.
He highlighted the joint action taken by police of several states and central agencies recently against the Pakistan-backed Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN), which has been designated a terror organisation under the unlawful activities prevention act or UAPA.
“More than 40 of its modules have been neutralised across the country. Over 100 cases have been registered and more than 271 arrests were made. The hallmark of a successful agency is to apprehend terrorists and put them behind bars even before they can execute a terrorist incident. The police in every state should analyse this model, accept it, and implement it in their respective areas,” the home minister said.
He also cited the dismantling of the Popular Front of India (PFI) network in September 2022 as an example of coordinated police action, in which cops from 11 states and central agencies had taken part.
Shah stressed on the need to dismantle terror financing networks, for which better coordination was required between agencies.
“We will not achieve success unless we strike at the entire terrorist network in a coordinated and comprehensive manner”.
He also asked for “greater emphasis on structural and operational capabilities”.
“The entire terrorist network must be investigated and its capabilities dismantled. By doing so, many incidents could be prevented. We need to develop a mechanism through which police station-level intelligence is transmitted through multiple levels to the Director General of Police (DGP), enabling the extraction of actionable intelligence. The Anti-Terrorism Squads (ATS) of every state need to strengthen their cyber expert units,” Shah said.
He also said that establishing a quadrangular regional security grid in border states should be a “key priority”.
The home minister said 303 fugitives had been brought back to India from 36 countries since 2019 as part of a special drive to secure the return of offenders, which was essential to eliminate terrorism, organised crime and drug-related offences.

articles.title: Goyal calls for trusted India-US supply chains
articles.text: New Delhi: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Thursday called for building resilient and trusted supply chains between India and the US amid prevailing global uncertainties.This helps countries reduce dependence on one geography, securing supplies of critical goods and strengthening India-US economic and strategic ties, the minister said.Addressing the Indo-US Economic Summit here, he said huge potential exists between the two countries to enhance economic cooperation, as the US offers capital, technology, and innovation, while India offers skills, talent, manufacturing strength, and competitiveness.Goyal said he would conclude with five calls to action, using the acronym TRUST to outline his suggestions."T - the first letter. Let us turn our supply chains into resilient and trusted supply chains. 'R', let us raise our talent together with our friendly and partner countries," he said.The minister suggested increasing collaborations between Indian and US universities."I am working with some of them to bring them to India. We'd like to invite all US universities and students to look at India as a part of their program. Because I firmly believe global growth is going to be led from countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America. And time spent by students from the developed world in Indian universities and Indian colleges will help them learn how to deal with us," he added.He said 'S' in the TRUST acronym stands for 'Speak', urging both sides to communicate candidly and openly flag any hurdles or difficulties they face."Let us Speak to each other candidly. Let us flag off the hurdles or the difficulties that anybody faces. So that we can work as your partners to help you in your work. We have different arms of the government which will support you in your work. And help you take your work, take your business to the world," Goyal said.He said the final 'T' stood for 'Track', emphasising the need to monitor outcomes, ensure accountability for performance and urging the IACC to hold both sides accountable.He added that India and the US are two vibrant democracies which shape the global narrative and are important engines for global growth."...an engine always runs on fuel, and that fuel, when it comes to India, is trust. India offers a trusted partnership. India offers our trust, a partner who will stand by you through thick and thin. In every crisis, India is that one partner which never lets its friends down," he added.In a volatile and uncertain world, countries face challenges due to the ongoing wars and the West Asia crisis."In these uncertain times, the world no longer needs just supply chains. They need trusted supply chains. In a trust chain, the partner shares your vision, respects the rule of law, honours contracts and therefore India and the US are natural links who build a chain of trust, a trusted chain. These strong bonds are reflected in our engagement at every level," the minister noted.The minister said the country's exports of goods and services have reached an all-time high of USD 90 billion."That is the India growth story. And that is the story we wish to share with our friends like the United States of America," he added.Meanwhile, speaking at the FICCI event, Goyal said that the country would achieve the USD one trillion exports target during the current fiscal.He added that India must move beyond reducing its dependence on the world and instead make the world dependent on India.He urged FICCI to remake itself as a global chamber at its centenary celebrations.The country, Goyal said, now has the capital, talent, entrepreneurs and banking strength to raise its ambition."Last time I came to your AGM, I spoke about reducing dependence on the world and becoming self-reliant. Today I would like to suggest going one step forward," he said, adding, "We need to make the world dependent upon us. articles.title: CBSE moves Supreme Court to recall Class 6 exemption from three-language policy
articles.text:
CBSE moves Supreme Court to recall Class 6 exemption from three-language policy
The CBSE has sought recall of the Supreme Court order exempting Class 6 students from the three-language policy, saying it affects academic arrangements.
The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has approached the Supreme Court seeking recall of the September 28 order exempting Class VI students from the three-language policy for the current academic year claiming that the order will apply to less than 1% of the students studying in Standard VI across the CBSE schools in the country.
The application filed on Wednesday states that out of a total of over 2.344 million students studying in Standard VI of CBSE schools, 99.82% of the students (over 2.340 million) are already studying two native languages. The exemption, according to the Board, will benefit 4,186 students throughout the country (about 0.18%) studying two foreign languages.
Additional solicitor general (ASG) Aishwarya Bhati appearing for Centre told a bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Thursday that the matter requires some “ironing out” and requested for an early hearing on the application. The court agreed to hear the matter next week.
While issuing the September 28 order, the court had said that since the exemption from the policy is already available to students of Classes VII, VIII and IX, the same “comfort” should be extended to Class VI students as well.
The order was passed despite the court being told by the Centre that 98-99% of the schools have been provided adequate facilities for implementation of the third language policy and only 1.2% schools are yet to provide such facilities. The order said, “We direct that the students, who are in 6th standard, may be granted the same exemption as has been granted to the students of the 7th standard.”
Long before the three-language policy of CBSE was introduced under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 for Class VI in April 2026, the Board said that CBSE affiliated schools have been offering two native languages in Classes VI to VIII for the past several decades. These schools have adequate facilities to teach two native languages, it stated, adding that the third language concept was introduced only in Standard IX for the first time this year.
The data provided by the Board indicates a total of 1,466,682 schools (CBSE and non-CBSE) in the country having a total enrolment of 247,219,766 students. Of these, 33,017 schools in the country are affiliated with CBSE, collectively to over 27.5 million students from Standard I to XII. Since the present case before the court concerns only CBSE schools, the Board said the schools offering two foreign languages in Standard VI are 99 catering to 4,186 students. In these schools, 19,892 students are pursuing two native languages.
Relying on this data, the CBSE said, “The perception being created that the schools teaching foreign languages do not have facilities to teach native languages is wrong... There is no shortfall in terms of requisite arrangements for teaching of two native languages in all CBSE schools in Class VI.” In other words, all schools affiliated to CBSE do teach two or more native languages, it added.
To make out a strong case, the CBSE gathered data of students currently in Class VII pursuing two foreign languages. Evidently, they had pursued this choice in Class VI as well. Now, the strength of such students had reduced to 4,186 with the rest of the approximately 45,000 students having opted for two native languages in Class VI in the current year.
The Board said, “Any relaxation given to Class VI students to protect the interest of only 4,186 students would be unfair to those approximately 45,000 students who have availed of the existing facility in their schools and have opted for two native languages.”
Such relaxation has also created an uncertainty in the academic arrangements already made by all CBSE schools, it added.
The petitions challenging the three-language policy were filed by students and parents of CBSE schools claiming that the introduction of policy mid-stream raised uncertainty among students and posed questions of preparedness with regard to curriculum, books, and availability of teachers.
The Board had earlier told the court that Class VI textbooks for the third language in all 22 scheduled Indian languages were available on the NCERT website, covering the choices of over 98% of schools. For the remaining languages, SCERT textbooks and resources would be used.
On teacher availability, the CBSE said about 93% of the 20,777 schools already had teachers for at least two distinct indigenous languages. Of these, 3,523 schools had teachers for three or more such languages.
The Centre had formed a five-member committee on September 16 to facilitate and monitor implementation of the three-language framework in Classes VI to X. The committee headed by education ministry director Bhagwati Prasad Kalal also has NCERT secretary Rajeev Kumar, CBSE director (academics) Praggya M Singh, KVS additional commissioner Chandana Mandal and NVS deputy commissioner Somvir Poonia.

articles.title: Russian national accused of stalking San Francisco techie in plot against US defense-tech giant
articles.text:
A Russian national is being held in custody after being arrested for allegedly spying on a US defense tech company in Palo Alto, shoulder-surfing employees, and dropping remote surveillance devices at their homes.

Igor D'iu was indicted after FBI agents surveilled his activities between June and October 2026, which they say were issued as "tasks" from what is thought to be Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB), according to an affidavit [PDF] signed by an FBI special agent.

After FBI agents secured a warrant to raid D'iu's temporary premises in October, they say that Telegram messages harvested from his seized devices confirmed investigators' findings and revealed that he was spying on an unnamed company.

Court documents describe the company in question as a large technology and defense company with offices in Palo Alto, and media-reported links to the Russia-Ukraine war.

While unconfirmed officially, the company has widely been reported as Palantir, which did not respond to our request for confirmation.

D'iu allegedly received instructions from Telegram contacts, whom he only suspected were representatives of the Russian government, weeks after entering the US illegally in July.

The indictment alleges he was ordered to surveil employees' homes, take photographs of their screens while working remotely at coffee shops, and permit his handlers to remotely access his laptop for the purpose of capturing data from nearby devices owned by the company’s employees.

In some cases, the filing alleges, D’iu was asked to leave a laptop outside one employee's apartment complex, all while allowing his Telegram handlers to remotely operate the device.

The first time, he was asked to leave the laptop for one hour while the handlers worked, and another time, he was told to drop it off in the middle of the night and only come back to collect it three hours later, the filing claims.

D'iu is also allegedly to have followed two female employees in his rented car, driving dangerously and violating multiple road laws to do so.

One of the two employees was followed briefly, but D'iu followed another for nearly 30 miles, according to the affidavit signed by FBI special agent Winston Wong.

D'iu was said to have followed the woman as she performed U-turns, illegal left turns, ran red lights, navigated via back and side streets, and through grocery store parking lots.

The car following her only peeled away after the woman drove to the San Francisco Mission police station on the advice of a 911 call handler.

Questioned about the incident, which according to police reports caused the woman significant emotional distress, D'iu confirmed he was the driver but claimed he was following her to ask her out on a date.

Inside recruitment

The affidavit did not detail the suspect's background beyond his alleged offenses in the US earlier this year, although it mentioned Russian intelligence's history of recruiting "criminal proxies, organized crime groups, and other disposable agents" to carry out operations.

According to the FBI's account, D'iu entered the US illegally – without relevant visas – in either June or July 2026. Travel records obtained on September 10 showed that his last recorded journey was from Istanbul to Mexico City. There was no record of him entering the US.

Investigators would later come to know that he travelled on that Istanbul-Mexico City flight on June 7, allegedly using a ticket provided to him by one of the three contacts from whom he received orders via Telegram.

A Facebook account, registered using a Mexican +528 number and D'iu's name, posted on June 30 asking for help getting "closer to New York," adding that "I'll pay as much as needed." The account replied to a response from someone who told him to contact a Mexico phone number on WhatsApp.

The filing claims the first mobile phone signals associated with D'iu's devices did not ping US towers until a month later, on July 31, suggesting he did not arrive in the US - specifically McAllen, Texas - until around that date. Telegram messages would also go on to confirm that he was allegedly helped across the border by an "Uzbek contact" in Mexico.

Records obtained from Google showed D'iu created a Google account in April. According to the affidavit, D'iu used it to search for the company's Wikipedia page on July 28, and on August 3, used Google's AI to devise a route around Texas that bypassed border checkpoints.

The FBI believes D'iu's "spying" began in mid-August, after he bought a laptop, a Wi-Fi device, a puck device, and an additional phone. At this point, the agency claims, he had received his first order to visit a coffee shop near the Palo Alto company’s office and snap employees' laptop screens before sending copies back to his handlers.

Three days later, D'iu was ordered to go back to a coffee shop and allow his Telegram contacts to remotely control the laptop and collect data from employee devices that were in range, claims the filing.

D'iu was paid $15,000 on three occasions between August 12 and October 6, according to the court documents. To verify the transaction, he was told to send a picture of a dollar bill's serial number to the Telegram contacts, along with a description of what he was wearing. A courier would then arrive, confirming the serial number and handing D'iu the cash.

The filing alleges he used this money to purchase the tech equipment, accommodation, and travel, including a rented silver 2026 Lexus RX 350 from a private owner in Los Angeles on August 22, which he is said to have driven back to San Francisco.

The same Lexus was captured on security footage outside the unnamed company's office on September 1, and over the following two days was implicated in the two instances of female employees being followed.

Contacted by Palo Alto police on September 4, D'iu confirmed he was the driver who dangerously followed the female staffer for nearly 30 minutes, but claimed he knew nothing about the nearby businesses. D'iu would then claim he followed the woman because he thought she was beautiful and wanted to ask her out on a date, and denied following anyone else.

The affidavit goes on to allege that D'iu then traveled to Reno, Nevada, to lay low after his run-in with the police. He spent the time trying to reroute DHL deliveries from San Francisco to his hideout address, which US Customs would later intercept.

These ended up containing fake IDs with the images the DoJ claims matched D'iu's, including Uzbek documents, a US passport whose number belonged to a New York woman, and a social security card registered to a "Hugo Landry Johns."

He traveled back to the Bay Area in late September, swapping his silver Lexus for a white 2016 Dodge Challenger, and received additional instructions from his handlers, including the order to leave a remote-controlled laptop outside the apartment complex, says the filing.

One Telegram contact named Ian Morales sent photos of at least four employees and their addresses, along with instructions for D'iu to dress as a food delivery worker and visit those locations, asking whoever answered to verify they lived there.

FBI agents executed a search warrant on October 8, seizing a cache of evidence, including what they listed as being:

  • The forged ID documents

  • Two Russian passports

  • $18,035 in cash

  • Two laptops

  • Two iPhones

  • Two T-Mobile SIM cards

  • Wi-Fi equipment

  • A notebook with 10 handwritten addresses supplied by Telegram contacts, along with times the suspect was supposed to attend those locations, at least five of which were for company employees’ homes

  • Profile packages for at least three employees, including: Names, personal information, education and employment histories, names of relatives, narrative histories, and assessments of leadership qualities, strengths, and weaknesses.

Suspicions and charges

Per the affidavit, D'iu was said to have only become suspicious of the tasks he was being ordered to complete in October, when his handlers ordered the laptop to be dropped near the apartment complex.

"D'iu gradually began to understand he was doing something bad and that his actions were illegal," the affidavit stated.

At this point, he allegedly asked the Telegram contacts who he was working for, to which they replied "the Motherland," and the company he was surveilling was involved in providing weapons to Ukraine, resulting in D’iu suspecting the Russian government.

Wong said in the affidavit: "Based on my training, experience, and research, D'iu's communications with his Telegram contacts is consistent with the tactics of [Russian intelligence] and its criminal proxies for spotting, assessing, recruiting, and handling intelligence assets and sources.

"D'iu's targeting of the company and its employees is also consistent with [Russian intelligence] objectives in Russia's war against Ukraine."

The Russian national was indicted and charged with two counts related to spying offences, and one count related to the fake identity documents. He is next due in court on November 24 but remains in federal custody. ®

articles.title: Scientists flooded GTA’s Los Santos to simulate rising seas
articles.text:
Scientists flooded GTA’s Los Santos to simulate rising seas
They used a fan-built 3D model of the map, and pinned it to coordinates with 11 control points and set the sea level from 31 shoreline points
The water reached Vespucci’s canals first. Then the Port of South Los Santos stopped working, followed by the gasworks and the sewage plant. Nobody in a stolen car caused any of this. The sea simply came in. That’s Los Santos, the sunbathed in-game version of Los Angeles of Grand Theft Auto V, in the face of a rising seas scenario modelled by Paul Nörenberg and Hugues Lantuit of the University of Potsdam and the Alfred Wegener Institute. Their paper coincides with the launch of the GTA VI video game. Los Santos, they say, serves as an ideal case study because it faithfully replicates the real Los Angeles, thereby enabling a direct comparison of simulated flood outcomes.
The scientists are working with two Representative Concentration Pathway (RCP) scenarios from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Fifth Assessment Report (AR5). The researchers used these scenarios to simulate the consequences of any future sea-level rise and demonstrate the exact ways the city in GTA V would change.
The research notes that under the RCP 8.5 scenario with storm surges, combined sea levels are projected to reach 5.18 m by 2300, with the model showing 5.1 % of the mapped land area inundated; for a 2500 scenario with projected sea levels of 8.22 mm, this increases to 6.5 % modelled inundation, which places the port, wastewater infrastructure, and coastal energy facilities at risk. Under the RCP 2.6 mitigation scenario, the model shows 2.2 % of land area inundated at 2300 with storm surge, with no major infrastructure affected.
“Many games have now advanced graphically to such an extent that they can reproduce real-world locations almost true to life,” says Paul Nörenberg, lead author of the study. Grand Theft Auto V (GTA V) is one of those games: it takes players to the fictional city of Los Santos. “The city is a near-exact replica of the real-life Los Angeles, with all its famous landmarks, neighbourhoods as well as urban and coastal features.”
In 2017, four scientific modelling teams, from the Netherlands, US, Japan and Austria, coordinated through the Integrated Assessment Modeling Consortium (IAMC) to create four scenarios, which the United Nations’ IPCC published.
Rockstar doesn’t release any raw terrain data. The scientists used a fan-built 3D model of the map, pinned it to coordinates with 11 control points and set the sea level from 31 shoreline points. This was checked by flying an in-game helicopter along the coastline. The height was calibrated against the game’s Mount Chiliad. They then simulated the IPCC scenarios for the years 2100, 2300 and 2500—each topped with a 1.59-metre storm surge, the highest Los Angeles has ever recorded.
When the scientists overlaid the simulation data over real maps and flood studies for Los Angeles, the same districts in reality also stood most exposed. Vespucci floods like Venice Beach might, Chumash like Malibu, and the Port of South Los Santos is as vulnerable as the Port of LA. Rockstar Games, the developer, copied the city closely enough to inadvertently replicate its weak spots.
Rockstar Games says GTA V is the second best-selling video game of all time, with more than 225 million copies sold in the last decade. There is a large community of players familiar with Los Santos.
“If this familiar, personally explored virtual landscape changes, players can engage with the effects of climate change on an emotional level,” notes Nörenberg. “This can bridge a gap in a way that conventional visualisations, such as models or maps, struggle to achieve.”
The scientists agree this isn’t without caveats. “We recommend the approach as a template for geoscience communication using open-world video game environments, with the explicit caveat that the static inundation model and its limitations must be communicated transparently to every audience, and that the 2300 and 2500 horizons remain the weakest part of the scenario set,” they say.
A commercial video game is built for storytelling and action, not exactly for rigorous scientific modelling. The terrain is often simplified and static water levels often cannot replicate finer natural nuances such as coastal erosion, drainage systems, or shifting weather patterns.
The template, may have given scientists a new avenue. As game studios spend billions building realistic virtual twins of real cities, scientists now have a real-world utility for those maps.

articles.title: India proposes joint vision document ahead of Nepal PM Balen Shah’s visit next week
articles.text:
India proposes joint vision document ahead of Nepal PM Balen Shah’s visit next week
India has proposed a joint vision document covering trade, investment, energy and connectivity ahead of Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah’s visit on November 22.
India has proposed a joint vision document focused on economic cooperation, investment, transit, energy, digital connectivity and health to be unveiled during Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah’s visit to India next week as part of efforts to take forward a reset of bilateral relations, people familiar with the matter said.
The rapper-turned-politician, who has shied away from foreign trips since he became PM in March, is set to travel to India for a visit lasting a little more than 24 hours, arriving on November 22 and departing the following day. The visit is yet to be formally announced by both sides.
Ahead of the trip, Kathmandu has conveyed a proposal for a $2 billion economic package, including $1 billion in grants, as part of efforts to take forward development projects and reconstruct areas affected by the Bhote Koshi flash floods, the people said.
Shah’s visit is being seen as an opportunity for a reset in bilateral ties and is expected to focus on economic matters, air, land and digital connectivity, improved border management, and employment and educational opportunities. It will also be an opportunity for him to get to know India’s top leadership, the people said.
As part of the reset in relations, the Indian side proposed the joint vision document, to be formally adopted at the conclusion of the visit, which will focus on long-term cooperation and targets in specific sectors such as economic cooperation and trade, investment, transit, energy, digital connectivity, health, education and people-to-people ties, the people said. The document will also consolidate existing cooperation and set targets for India-backed development projects, they said.
India’s new ambassador to Nepal, Sudhakar Dalela, met Shah in Kathmandu on Wednesday and discussed ways to advance bilateral ties and cooperation. Dalela also briefed Shah on preparations for the high-level visit, the Indian embassy said.
The people referred to Nepal’s proposal for a $2 billion economic package and said detailed project reports would be required for financial grants and soft loans. They said that an assessment would also have to be made of Nepal’s ability to absorb and utilise such grants and loans. At the same time, they pointed out that India has not rolled out such a massive economic package in one go for any of its partners.
Leaders of Nepal’s ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP), which came to power in elections held after a Gen Z uprising in 2025 that unseated the government of KP Sharma Oli, have repeatedly said they are not burdened with historical baggage and want a relationship with India that focuses on concrete outcomes, including the need to create economic opportunities and provide additional air connectivity.

articles.title: Kerala CBI court convicts 13 in 2012 MSF activist murder, acquits CPI(M) leaders Jayarajan, Rajesh
articles.text:
Kerala CBI court convicts 13 in 2012 MSF activist murder, acquits CPI(M) leaders Jayarajan, Rajesh
A CBI court in Ernakulam convicted 13 CPI(M) activists in the 2012 murder of MSF worker Ariyil Abdul Shukoor, while acquitting P Jayarajan and TV Rajesh.
A special Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) court in Ernakulam on Thursday convicted 13 CPI(M) activists in the 2012 murder of Muslim Students Federation (MSF) activist Ariyil Abdul Shukoor, sentencing seven of them to life imprisonment, while acquitting 18 others, including senior party leaders P Jayarajan and TV Rajesh, of conspiracy charges.
Jayarajan is a CPI(M) state committee member and former Kannur district secretary, while Rajesh is a former two-time MLA from the district.
The court awarded life imprisonment to seven of the 13 convicts who were found guilty of murder. Six other convicts were sentenced to jail terms of up to two years for various offences.
Dawood Muhammed, brother of the victim, told reporters that the special court’s ruling was disappointing with regard to the acquittal of the two senior party leaders.
“The eyewitnesses knew about the consequences they could face if they spoke against the man (Jayarajan) who has been at the forefront of Kannur’s murder politics. The accused were influential and the witnesses faced lifelong threats. I cannot understand why the court did not accept the conspiracy charges despite ample evidence. We will certainly challenge the acquittal,” he said.
However, Jayarajan said the conspiracy charge against him and Rajesh was a result of a plot hatched by the Congress-IUML leadership, who were in power at the time.
“Under pressure from the ruling parties then, police officers investigating the case were played like puppets. A conspiracy theory (involving me) was floated. That conspiracy theory collapsed in today’s verdict,” Jayarajan said.
The convicts who were sentenced to life imprisonment on Thursday were identified as KV Sumesh, AV Anoop, Pavithran, Manoharan, Dinesan, Bijumon and Shijin Mohan. The six other convicts who received lesser jail sentences were EP Radhakrishnan, KV Sajith, VV Mohanan, MV Purushothaman, PK Ajithkumar and PP Sureshan.
Shukoor, 24, was hacked to death by assailants near Kannapuram in Kannur district on February 20, 2012, triggering widespread protests at the time. He was associated with MSF, the student wing of IUML. Shukoor’s murder followed intense clashes between the CPI(M) and IUML in the Pattuvam area of the politically volatile northern district of the state.
The prosecution argued that Shukoor was targeted by the CPI(M) in retaliation for an attack on a vehicle carrying Jayarajan and Rajesh by IUML workers. It claimed during the trial that the conspiracy to target Shukoor was hatched in a room at the cooperative hospital in Taliparamba in the presence of Rajesh and Jayarajan.
Home minister Ramesh Chennithala said the government would hold discussions with the victim’s family before deciding on the future course of legal action. Kerala chief minister V D Satheesan said justice must be delivered to Shukoor’s family, who have suffered immensely as a result of the political vendetta of the CPI(M) leadership. “The Government stands firmly with the family and will pursue every available legal avenue to ensure that justice is served,” he said in a post on X.
